Andorra.note: Read law27/2017; government catalogue also identifies Llei24/2025: https://www.govern.ad/es/tematiques/habitatge/normativa . Current consolidated requirements unresolved.

Austria.note: Reader failed once; search metadata only.
Austrian Standards lists ÖVE/ÖNORM EN 301549 V3.2.1, issued on 1 May 2021, referring to EN 301 549 V3.2.1:2021 (source notation 2021-03).

Belgium.note: Agency accessibility statement is a lead to legislation, not consolidated legal text.

The NSSO accessibility statement for Working in Belgium refers to EN 301 549 when reporting partial website compliance. This is a website-specific reference, not a national standards-adoption finding.

Bosnia and Herzegovina.note: Ministry overview; retrieve consolidated instrument separately.
ISBIH’s 2022 bulletin lists BAS EN 301 549 V3.2.1:2022 and identifies EN 301 549 V3.2.1:2021 as identical (IDT).

Bulgaria.note: Legislation catalogue; provisions and current amendments not audited.

The Bulgarian State Reserve’s accessibility declaration identifies BDS EN 301549:2021 and EN 301 549 V3.2.1:2021 as applicable standards for its website assessment. This is an agency website reference.

China, Hong Kong Special Administrative.note: Historical verified-legislation list search lead; retrieve current ordinance.
Generic export-market testing-service marketing on Hong Kong locale page; no domestic adoption or procurement connection established.

China, Macao Special Administrative Regi.note: Reader failed; architectural-barrier law metadata only; current status unresolved.

Cook Islands.note: Official complaint guidance; obtain complete current Act.

Croatia.note: Secondary source; obtain official Narodne novine text.
HZN’s repository lists HRN EN 301 549 V3.2.1:2021 for ICT accessibility requirements.

Cyprus.note: Search metadata only; current text not read.
EU representation website lead, not national standard adoption; one failed retrieval.

Czechia.note: Secondary text; reconcile against official collection.

The Czech Standardization Agency lists ČSN EN 301549 among standards supporting accessibility of products and services. That row gives no edition; adjacent rows separately list ČSN ETSI EN 301 549 V3.1.1 and V3.2.1.

Democratic People's Republic of Korea.note: International mission report; primary national law text and current status unresolved.

Denmark.note: Reader returned no substantive text; historical consolidation.
Danish Standards makes DS/ETSI EN 301 549 V3.2.1:2021 available in Danish and English for public bodies under its agreement with the Agency for Digital Government.

Estonia.note: EVS lists EVS-EN 301 549 V4.1.1:2026 as valid from 16 September 2026, based on EN 301 549 V4.1.1. This catalogue date is not a legal commencement finding.

Faroe Islands.note: Title/header dates differ; no exact date or legal-effect claim recorded.
Search snippet lists foreign regulatory examples; local relationship unresolved and no full read completed.

Finland.note: English translation completed2015; later amendments unresolved.
Traficom’s guidance on the Act on the Provision of Digital Services identifies EN 301 549 as the standard defining its technical accessibility requirements and links an SFS edition.

France.note: Original Gazette section; not a current consolidated audit.
The French government’s RGAA reference page links EN 301 549 V2.1.2:2018 in French and English. This establishes a reference in that guidance, not the latest applicable national edition.

Germany.note: Source identified; no provision-level currentness claim.
DIN Media lists DIN EN 301549:2022-06 with EN 301 549 V3.2.1:2021 (source notation 2021-03) as its English version.

Greece.note: Reader failed once; law remains search lead.
An ELOT telecommunications-standardization presentation lists ELOT EN 301 549 among example ETSI standards. The cited slide does not specify an edition.

Hungary.note: Reader failed once; law remains search lead.
MSZT states that it published the Hungarian-language version of MSZ EN 301 549:2020 on 1 December 2020. The underlying EN version and subsequent national editions require separate checking.

Ireland.note: Reader failed once; original enacted version lead.
Ireland’s National Disability Authority refers to EN 301 549 V3.2.1 in its guidance on public-body websites and mobile applications under the Web Accessibility Directive.

Italy.note: Search metadata only; consolidation not read.
UNI’s catalogue lists UNI CEI EN 301549:2021 for ICT accessibility requirements. The underlying EN version is not identified in the retrieved catalogue text.

Kosovo.note: Search metadata only; consolidated law not checked.

Latvia.note: Source read for identity; legal applicability not audited.
LVS lists LVS EN 301549:2022 L in Latvian and identifies ETSI EN 301 549 V3.2.1:2021 (source notation 2021-03) among its source documents.

Liechtenstein.note: Version metadata only; amendments and current provisions unresolved.
The Liechtenstein administration’s accessibility statement refers to EN 301 549 V3.2.1:2021 (source notation 2021-03) when reporting partial website compliance. This is a website-specific reference.

Search indicates EN reference; two failed PDF reads prevent passage verification.

Luxembourg.note: Agency statement links law; no legal interpretation recorded.

Website statement EN search lead; two failed reads.

Monaco.note: Reader failed once; title retained as discovery metadata.

Montenegro.note: Publication landing page; do not confuse newer draft search hit with enacted law.

Netherlands (Kingdom of the).note: Search metadata available; robots restriction prevents reader access.
NEN’s catalogue lists NEN-EN 301549:2021, published on 1 June 2021. The retrieved metadata does not identify the underlying EN version.

Niue.note: Media lead on policy review; reader failed; not a verified enacted law.

Bulletin contains MKS101550:2015 and EN in related-report title, but section and document status were not resolved; defer country connection.

UKE’s standards page refers to EN 301 549 V3.2.1:2021 and links its Polish translation in PKN’s catalogue. This records the page’s reference, not a finding about the latest edition.

Two failed reads of agency guidance; observatory reader returned empty content; references remain unverified.

Slovakia.note: Legal-source identity only; version-specific requirements not audited.

The Slovak standards office hosts a preview of STN EN 301 549 V1.1.2:2015. Its cover states that it includes the English version of the European Standard; latest national status requires separate checking.

Slovenia.note: Unofficial consolidated text hosted by official portal; follow its disclaimer.
Slovenia’s Information Society Inspectorate refers to SIST EN 301 549 V3.2.1 in its January 2025 notice on free access to standards.

Spain.note: Dated2023version; current consolidation requires separate check.
UNE’s February 2022 magazine lists UNE-EN 301549 among new standards for ICT accessibility requirements. The cited article does not identify the underlying EN version.

Sweden.note: Source identity only; no current provision-level interpretation.
Sweden’s National Procurement Services lists EN 301 549 among its guidance documents for accessibility in public procurement. The cited passage does not specify an edition.

Tuvalu.note: Policy catalogue only; distinguish2018policy and later unendorsed revision leads.

Ukraine.note: Historical summary reader failed; obtain full current text.
UNDP’s Ukraine article identifies DSTU EN 301 549:2022 as a Ukrainian standard duplicating the European standard. The underlying EN version and current legal requirements require separate checking.
